approved: ASIC Supervisory Cost Recovery Levy (Collection) Bill 2017
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill is part of a package that would introduce an industry funding model for ASIC starting 1 July 2017.
Under the model, ASIC would be required to annually explain its regulatory priorities and resource allocation, and improve its data collection from financial entities.
The package is expected to improve the budget balance by $308.7 million over the four years to 2020-21.
The bills would create an industry funding model for ASIC.
ASIC would be required to increase accountability through annual explanations of priorities and resource use.
ASIC would need to improve its collection and use of data from financial entities.
ASIC and the financial services sector, including consumers and regulated entities.

The ASIC Supervisory Cost Recovery Levy (Collection) Bill 2017 was introduced to implement an industry funding model requiring all ASIC-regulated entities to pay levies offsetting regulatory costs. Unpaid levies attract 20 per cent annual penalty interest, mandatory activity reporting is required with failure to report an offence, and dishonest reporting incurs a shortfall penalty of twice the levy avoided.
